title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): C is a k-linear category of 'bimodules' half-simplicial (semi-simplicial) objects, and C_0 is the additive subcategory of the ∂-perfect ones. In C_0 there is a totally acyclic cochain complex Φ^0→Φ^1→… with an 'ordered' Hom pattern: Hom(Φ^i,Φ^j) = k·id if j=i, k·∂_i if j=i+1, and 0 otherwise. The cycle objects are Ψ^i = Z^i(Φ^•). Each Φ^i sits in a canonical extension 0→Ψ^{i-1}→Φ^i→Ψ^i→0, and Hom(Ψ^i,Ψ^j) = δ_{ij} k. For a scalar u, L(i,u) is the pushout of this canonical extension along u·id on Ψ^{i-1}, so its class is u·e_i, where e_i is the class of Φ^i, and L(i,1)=Φ^i.

This page finishes the case j=i of computing Hom(L(i,n),L(i,m)).
- Any morphism α: L(i,n)→L(i,m) induces p·id on the sub-object Ψ^{i-1} and q·id on the quotient Ψ^i, because those endomorphism rings are k.
- A pair (p,q) lifts to some α exactly when p_*(class of source) = q^*(class of target) in Ext^1(Ψ^i,Ψ^{i-1}). This reads p·n·e_i = q·m·e_i, i.e. (qm − pn)e_i = 0.
- Hypothesis (C): e_i is a basis of Ext^1_{C_0}(Ψ^i,Ψ^{i-1}), so this group is ≅ k. The condition then becomes qm = pn.
- The solutions form a line, which Grothendieck parametrises with the reduced fraction m' = m/(m,n), n' = n/(m,n) and a parameter t∈k.
- For given (p,q) the lift α is unique, because two lifts differ by a map Ψ^i→Ψ^{i-1}, and Hom(Ψ^i,Ψ^{i-1}) = 0.
- Conclusion: Hom(L(i,n),L(i,m)) ≅ k.

The next page treats j=i−1 (giving 0) and j=i+1 (giving k, via the composite L(i,n)→Ψ^i→L(i+1,m)). This reproduces for the whole family L(i,u) the same 'directed', Ext-quiver-like Hom pattern that the Φ^i have.

Purpose: this is part of a dévissage (structure theory) of the category of ∂-perfect half-simplicial complexes. He is pinning down the indecomposable building blocks and the morphisms between them, presumably toward describing C_0 by a quiver with relations and then studying multiplicative structures.
errors: Inconsistency in the solution of qm = pn. From qm = pn one gets q/p = n/m, not m/n. The page writes q/p = m/n and then p = t n', q = t m', which satisfies qn = pm rather than qm = pn. With the stated condition the solutions are p = t m', q = t n'. The source of the mismatch is the garbled line 'q^*(e_{i,m}) = m e_i, p_*(e_{i,m}) = n e_i', which assigns m and n inconsistently to the two extensions. The result Hom ≅ k is unaffected.

The gcd normalisation (m,n) is meaningless over a field k. It only makes sense if the parameters are integers or k is something like Z or a PID. Over a field the solution line is simply k·(m,n), up to the swap noted above.

Gap or triviality not remarked on: over a field, any α with p,q ≠ 0 is an isomorphism by the five lemma. Hence L(i,n) ≅ L(i,m) ≅ Φ^i for all nonzero n,m, so the family L(i,u) collapses to a single object. The computation becomes meaningful only over a non-field base, where pushing out by u can change the isomorphism class, which may be why gcds appear.
The phrase 'Ext^1_{C_0}' assumes Ext^1 is computed inside the additive (possibly non-abelian) subcategory C_0. That requires C_0 to be closed under extensions in C, which is not stated here.

ideas.what: Classifying morphisms between extensions with prescribed scalar actions on sub and quotient via the condition p_* e = q^* e' in Ext^1, with uniqueness of the lift from Hom(quotient, sub) = 0.
ideas.modern_name: Morphisms of extensions / functoriality of Yoneda Ext (Baer pushout and pullback)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Baer, Yoneda; standard homological algebra (Cartan–Eilenberg, Mac Lane)

ideas.what: Hypothesis (C): Ext^1(Ψ^i,Ψ^{i-1}) is one-dimensional, spanned by the class of Φ^i, together with Hom(Ψ^i,Ψ^j) = δ_ij k. This is a directed, 'exceptional-like' configuration of objects.
ideas.modern_name: Exceptional sequences / directed (quasi-hereditary-like) Ext-quiver of type A with one arrow between consecutive vertices

missed.claim: As part of a 1975–76 dévissage of ∂-perfect half-simplicial bimodule complexes, Grothendieck singles out objects Φ^i, Ψ^i with exactly the Hom/Ext^1 pattern of an exceptional sequence with one-dimensional Ext between neighbours. He then computes Homs among the pushout family L(i,u). The local computation is routine. The broader programme — describing this category by a linear quiver with relations ∂∂ = 0, and adding multiplicative structures — is an unfinished thread, but this page alone contributes nothing new.
missed.quote: On fait l'hypothèse (C) | e_i est une base de Ext^1_{C_0}(Ψ^i, Ψ^{i-1})
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is only of historical interest: it is an early instance of exceptional-collection-style reasoning in Grothendieck's unpublished notes. It is not a new mathematical result.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine Yoneda-Ext computation of Hom between pushout extensions. It contains a minor swap error and over a field is essentially trivial, since all L(i,u) are isomorphic. Its only interest is contextual, as a fragment of an unpublished dévissage programme with an exceptional-sequence-like setup.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 should probably read 'q^*(e_{i,m}) = m e_i , p_*(e_{i,n}) = n e_i' (the two extensions L(i,m) and L(i,n)), not 'p_*(e_i, m)'.
The boxed hypothesis is 'e_i est une base de Ext^1_{C_0}(Ψ^i, Ψ^{i-1})', with the subscript C_0 under Ext.
In 'p = [-…-] t n'', the struck-out text is a crossed-out earlier attempt; the surviving text is p = t n', q = t m' (t ∈ k).
In 'Or tous p, q correspondant à un u', 'u' is likely 'α' (the morphism); the following line roughly reads 'qui est uniquement déterminé par (p,q)'.
The final line reads 'Hom(L(i,n), L(i,m)) ≃ k'.
